title: NEB Class 11 Physics — Ideal Gas — 2021
subject: physics
source: NEB Grade 11 Model Questions / NEB Past Papers 2020-2024

questions.question: What is the law of equipartition of energy? How many degrees of freedom does a monoatomic gas molecule have?
questions.solution:
The law states that energy is equally divided among all available degrees of freedom, each getting (1/2)kT of energy.

A monoatomic gas molecule has **3 translational degrees of freedom** (motion along x, y, z). Its molar specific heat at constant volume: Cv = (3/2)R.
questions.knowledgeNote: At thermal equilibrium, a monatomic gas has 3 translational degrees of freedom, a diatomic gas 5.
questions.answer: **Law of equipartition of energy:** in thermal equilibrium, the energy of a gas is **shared equally among all its degrees of freedom**, each degree of freedom receiving an average energy of **½kT per molecule** (½RT per mole), where k is the Boltzmann constant. **Monoatomic molecule:** it can only translate — motion along x, y and z — so it has **3 degrees of freedom**. (Hence average energy 3 × ½kT = 3kT/2 per molecule, and molar heat capacity C_v = 3R/2.) **Deep point:** a point-like atom has no way to store rotational or vibrational energy — that's why monatomic gases like helium have the lowest molar heat capacity of all gases.

questions.question: State Boyle's law and Charles's law and explain them with the $\mu$ notation.
questions.solution:
**Boyle's law:** At constant temperature, the pressure of a fixed mass of gas is **inversely proportional** to its volume.
$$P \propto \frac{1}{V} \;\Rightarrow\; \boxed{PV = \text{constant}} \;\Rightarrow\; P_1V_1 = P_2V_2$$
Graph of $P$ vs $V$ is a **rectangular hyperbola**; pressure increases when volume decreases. Follows Boyle's law $P \propto 1/V$; used in breathing and in the piston of an engine.

**Charles's law:** At constant pressure, the volume of a fixed mass of gas is **directly proportional** to its absolute temperature.
$$V \propto T \;\Rightarrow\; \boxed{\frac{V}{T} = \text{constant}} \;\Rightarrow\; \frac{V_1}{T_1} = \frac{V_2}{T_2}$$
Graph of $V$ vs $T$ is a **straight line through the origin**; the slope of $V$ vs $T$ (K) is the coefficient of cubical expansivity $\gamma = \dfrac{1}{V_0}\left(\dfrac{\Delta V}{\Delta T}\right)$.
questions.knowledgeNote: Boyle's law gives PV constant at constant temperature; Charles's law gives V proportional to T at constant pressure.
questions.answer: **Boyle's law:** at constant temperature (and fixed amount of gas), the pressure of a gas is inversely proportional to its volume — **PV = constant**, or P₁V₁ = P₂V₂ (isothermal). **Charles's law:** at constant pressure, the volume is directly proportional to the absolute temperature — **V/T = constant**, or V₁/T₁ = V₂/T₂ (isobaric). **With μ (amount of gas in moles):** both laws combine with Avogadro's principle into the ideal gas equation **PV = μRT** (R = 8.31 J/mol·K): Boyle's law is the special case μ, T fixed (PV = μRT = constant); Charles's law is the case μ, P fixed (V/T = μR/P = constant). Each gas law is the full equation with two of the three variables (P, V, T) held fixed. **Deep point:** PV = μRT is the single sentence containing all the gas laws — every 'law' is what remains when you freeze all but two of its letters.
